title: Epinephrine — Pediatric Anaphylaxis (IM)
sources: Wood JP, et al. Epinephrine for First-aid Management of Anaphylaxis. Pediatrics. 2017;139(3):e20164006.
International recommendations on epinephrine auto-injector doses often differ from standard weight-based guidance. Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol. 2022.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-15, fresh-look Batch 7). The existing peds-epinephrine-arrest card is IV/IO dosing for cardiac arrest; this is the distinct IM dosing/autoinjector-tier card for anaphylaxis, which uses a different route, concentration reference, and dosing cap.
Reformatted for reading on a phone: long paragraphs broken into short paragraphs and lists. Wording and clinical content unchanged.

purpose: IM epinephrine dosing for pediatric anaphylaxis — computed from exact weight for a manual draw-up, with the corresponding commercial autoinjector strength tier shown alongside for reference.

rule.repeat: May repeat every 5-15 minutes if inadequate response

doses.notes:
0.01 mg/kg of 1 mg/mL (1:1,000) IM — NOT the 0.1 mg/mL (1:10,000) concentration used for IV/IO cardiac arrest dosing.

Single-dose cap is commonly 0.3 mg in a prepubertal child, up to 0.5 mg in an adolescent/teen-sized patient — use clinical judgment on which cap applies near that transition.

If reaching for a commercial autoinjector instead of a manual draw-up:
- 7.5-15 kg = 0.1 mg autoinjector
- 15-30 kg = 0.15 mg
- ≥30 kg = 0.3 mg

Under 7.5 kg has no matching commercial autoinjector — use the computed manual IM dose above.

buildNote: drug-card schema, weight-based IM dosing (distinct route/concentration from the existing IV/IO peds-epinephrine-arrest card, which this card's own notes explicitly warn not to confuse). Commercial autoinjector weight tiers WebSearch-verified against Wood et al. (Pediatrics 2017) and a 2022 Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol review: 7.5-15 kg -> 0.1 mg autoinjector; 15-30 kg -> 0.15 mg; >=30 kg -> 0.3 mg (historical adult dose); under 7.5 kg has no matching commercial autoinjector and needs a manual weight-based draw-up, which is exactly what this card's computed dose is for. Autoinjector tiers are informational reference only — the schema's computed per-kg dose is the authoritative number for a manual draw-up.
